events.title: The death of Blessed Frances d'Amboise
events.shortBlurb: The widowed Duchess of Brittany, who had planted the first Carmel of nuns in France, laid down her rule and died in her own cloister at Nantes…
body: Born about 1427 at the castle of Thouars, Frances was the daughter of Louis d'Amboise, Viscount of Thouars. Betrothed as a small child to Peter, a younger son of John V, Duke of Brittany, she was married at fifteen in 1442. When Peter came to rule as Peter II in 1450, the pair were crowned in the cathedral of Rennes, and her charity so marked his short reign that chroniclers called it "the time of the blessed duchess."

Widowed and childless in 1457, she withstood the pressure of her family and of King Louis XI, who wished her to marry again, and turned instead to God. With Blessed John Soreth, prior general of the Carmelites, she founded in 1463 at Bondon near Vannes the first convent of Carmelite nuns in France, called "The Three Maries," its first sisters brought from Liège. She took the habit in 1468, was elected prioress in 1473, and later made a second foundation at Nantes.

She died on 4 November 1485 near Nantes and was long venerated as the foundress of the French Carmel. Pope Pius IX confirmed her cult in 1863, and her feast is kept on 4 November; images show her in the Carmelite habit with an ermine cloak to recall her rank.
